label: Latxa

names.text: Spanish Wikipedia (opened) uses the form lacha, as in lacha de cara negra and lacha de cara rubia. Lacho and Ardi latx were not seen on any page and are left out.

origin.place: The Basque Country (Biscay, Gipuzkoa, Navarre and Cantabria), Spain

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened): native to the Basque Country, mainly Biscay, Gipuzkoa, Navarre and Cantabria. No founding date is given.

about.text: The Latxa is a Basque dairy sheep kept in northern Spain. Its unpasteurized milk is used to make the Idiazabal and Roncal cheeses, and its long coarse wool is now largely a by-product.

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened): the dairy use for Idiazabal and Roncal and the wool as an agricultural by-product.
Wikipedia (opened): dairy use for the two cheeses. No meat use is mentioned there.

facts.v: About one litre of milk a day, over lactations of 140 days for the black-faced variety and 155 for the fair-faced.

sources.text: Spanish Wikipedia (opened). The per-lactation total is not stated on the page and is not worked out here.

facts.v: A breeding scheme with artificial insemination and machine milking has been in place since 1982.

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened), citing Gomez and Amezaga 2003 (FAO) and Georgoudis, Rosati and Mosconi 2005.

facts.v: Some farmers use hybrid Assaf sheep, which some say does not meet the requirements of the Idiazabal denomination of origin.

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened), citing Schmitt 2009 in The Atlantic.

gaps: No population count found on the pages or in search, so the head field is left out. The DAD-IS risk status was not found. Milk composition was not found. Litres per lactation were not found. The formation year was not found. Lacho and Ardi latx were not verified.
